desc: Read the integer N and the two strings S and T from standard input.

Verify the consistency condition: iterate through both strings and ensure that for every index i, if S[i] != T[i], then S[i] has not been mapped to a different character before (i.e., if S[i] == S[j] and i != j, then T[i] must equal T[j]). If this condition is violated, print -1.
If the condition holds, calculate the number of operations by counting the unique characters in S that are not already equal to their target in T.
Count the number of cycles in the functional graph formed by the mappings (excluding self-loops where map[c] == c).
Print the calculated count of operations (which is the sum of unique changing characters and the number of cycles).
Verify the logic with provided sample inputs manually or via dry run.
Ensure edge cases (e.g., S=T, no changes needed) are handled correctly (output 0).
Confirm the cycle counting logic handles disjoint cycles correctly.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
Test edge cases: N=1, S=T, S and T completely disjoint, large N.
If all pass, mark as solved.
